newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS to raise transatlantic fares.
newsitem.headline: SAS to raise transatlantic fares.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) SASbOL said on Friday that it would exploit rising fuel prices to raise air fares to the United States.

"We are considering doing some selective price rises related directly to fuel prices, but it will be on a selected basis," SAS senior vice-president Vagn Sorensen told Reuters during a conference on aviation law.
"One example, definitely, is that we will use the opportunity to raise the fares to the United States because they are chronically low," he said.
On other routes to and from Scandinavia, Sorensen said SAS would track its competitors' prices.
"We will probably be matching everything our competitors do into Scandinavia," he said.
Scope for increases within the carrier's home region of Denmark, Sweden and Norway -- where air fares are already among the world's highest -- were limited, he added.
"We are talking about one or two percent, we do not think it can take any more than that."
